jobs.title: ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST
jobs.description:
Job Posting: ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (00100762)

Department of Water Resources

JC-536356



ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (00100762)
  
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,551.00 - $9,787.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **12/7/2026**

### **Job Description and Duties**

The California Department of Water Resources (DWR) is seeking an Environmental Scientist to join our talented team of hydrographic science professionals in the Bathymetry Data Collection Section. This position is ideal for a dedicated professional who excels in dynamic outdoor field environments interested in operating sonar and other technical scientific data collection equipment, while possessing a strong analytical mindset for in-office data processing and analysis. The incumbent will be responsible for completing a variety of professional scientific duties as part of a Team involving the collection, processing, management, quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC), and analysis of bathymetric, hydrographic and other environmental and geographic information, generally within the Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta and at facilities related to the State Water Project. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong aptitude for boating and marine field work, experience operating advanced water science equipment including sonar technology, and a proactive approach to troubleshooting technical, mechanical, and electrical issues. In addition, the candidate will possess a keen interest in office based data processing, data investigations, spatial analysis and ability to prepare related exhibits and presentations using ArcGIS, CARIS, PowerPoint and related software.

At DWR, you will have the advantage of numerous resources to support your work and your professional growth, including training opportunities, state-of-the-art software applications and tools, and knowledgeable and professional colleagues to assist with project success. As an employee of DWR, your work is critical in the delivery of water to over 26 million Californians, as well as contributing to protecting our environment. We hope you’ll review the Duties and Desirable Qualifications below and apply for this great career opportunity to join our team.

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

  

### **Position Details**

**Job Code #:**

JC-536356

**Position #(s):**

846-300-0762-010

**Working Title:**

**ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (00100762)**

**Classification:**

ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,551.00 - $6,337.00 A

$5,531.00 - $7,718.00 B

$7,000.00 - $9,787.00 C

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**# of Positions:**

1

**Work Location:**

Yolo County

**Telework:**

In Office

**Job Type:**

Permanent, Full Time

### **Department Information**

**Division of Regional Assistance, North Central Region Office, Resources Assessment Branch/Bathymetry Data Collection Section, West Sacramento**

Department of Water Resources (DWR) was established in 1956 by the California State Legislature. We manage California’s water resources, systems, and infrastructure, including the State Water Project, in a responsible sustainable way.

At DWR, we are embedding climate change response into every project we undertake. We have set standards to help evaluate how each project incorporates climate resilience principles and ensure consistency across the Department. Our mission is to sustainably manage the water resources of California, in cooperation with other agencies, to benefit the state’s people and protect, restore, and enhance the natural and human environments.

DWR also strives to create a trusting and welcoming workplace where employees embrace diverse viewpoints and treat each other with civility and respect. An important component of DWR’s equal employment opportunity program centers around justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion.

Department Website: https://water.ca.gov/

Free virtual career consultation services including one-on-one DWR career consultations, application/resume review, tips for applying, and mock interviews, provided by DWR’s Recruitment and Workforce Planning section can now be scheduled via https://water.ca.gov/About/Careers.

### **Special Requirements**

Possession of a valid California driver license is required. Possessing or obtaining a California Boater Card will also be required. The fieldwork described above will require driving and walking on public and private roadways and on uneven terrain and the ability to bend, stoop, twist, traverse and lift loads up to approximately 50 pounds. Candidates should be able to work on and around swift moving waterways.

  

All employees are responsible for contributing to an inclusive, safe, and secure work environment that values diverse cultures, perspectives, and experiences, and is free from discrimination.

### **Application Instructions**

Completed applications and all required documents must be received or postmarked by the Final Filing Date in order to be considered. Dates printed on Mobile Bar Codes, such as the Quick Response (QR) Codes available at the USPS, are not considered Postmark dates for the purpose of determining timely filing of an application.

Final Filing Date: 12/7/2026

Who May Apply

Individuals who are currently in the classification, eligible for lateral transfer, eligible for reinstatement, have list or LEAP eligibility, are in the process of obtaining list eligibility, or have SROA and/or Surplus eligibility (please attach your letter, if available). SROA and Surplus candidates are given priority; therefore, individuals with other eligibility may be considered in the event no SROA or Surplus candidates apply.
  
  
Applications will be screened and only the most qualified applicants will be selected to move

jobs.title: Senior Health Scientist, Environmental Health
jobs.description:
**About the role:**

The Environmental Public Health and Water team supports Victoria's Chief Health Officer Group in providing specialist expertise on the public health impacts of environmental hazards. The work is interesting and diverse and can involve dealing with unusual and unexpected or emerging environmental hazards and scenarios. The team provides advice on risk management, policy options and complex environmental public health issues, working under the Public Health and Wellbeing Act 2008, Public Health and Wellbeing Regulations 2019, Safe Drinking Water Act 2003, Safe Drinking Water Regulations 2025 and Health (Fluoridation) Act 1973.

This position is responsible for providing specialist health risk advice typically relating to environmental hazards, developing and implementing policies, supporting and/or co-ordinating the response to issues, investigations, incidents and emergencies, and for contributing to state and national level environmental health-related policies and guidelines. It also supports relevant national committees and management and leadership responsibilities when required.

**About us:**

At the Victorian Department of Health we want a future where Victorians are the healthiest people in the world. A Victoria where our children and people thrive, our workplaces are productive and safe, and our communities are more connected.

We see it as our job to support Victorians to stay healthy and safe. And to deliver a world-class healthcare system that ensures every single Victorian can access safe, quality care that leads to better health outcomes for all.

**About you:**

**Qualifications / Specialist Expertise:**

* A tertiary qualification in fields related especially to toxicology, or to environmental public health or health and environmental sciences is highly desirable.
* Demonstrated knowledge of risks to human health from environmental hazards and expertise in risk assessment, risk communication and risk management.

**What we offer:**

* The opportunity to perform meaningful work, making direct contributions toward enabling Victorians to be the healthiest people in the world.
* A wide range of growth and development opportunities within the department and wider Victorian Public Service.
* A strong commitment to work-life balance, including a diverse array of flexible working arrangements.

**How to apply:**

Applications should include a resume and a cover letter. Click the `Apply' button to view further information about the role including key contact details and the advertisement closing date.

We are committed to developing and supporting a workforce that is well equipped and highly motivated to provide responsive and quality services to all Victorians. We continue to build an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity of backgrounds and differences to realise the potential of our employees for innovation and delivering services aimed at enhancing the lives of all Victorians. All roles can be worked flexibly and we encourage applications from Aboriginal people, people with disability, LGBTIQ+ and people from culturally diverse backgrounds. Please contact us if you require any adjustments to participate in the recruitment process at inclusion@health.vic.gov.au. For more information on our commitment to inclusion and diversity see inclusion and diversity at the Department of Health.

If you have any queries in relation to participation in recruitment processes at Health, or experience any issues in applying, please feel free to email talentacquisition@health.vic.gov.au. Please note that unsolicited applications from third parties cannot be accepted. If you have questions regarding the role, please message the contact person listed on the advertisement directly.

Preferred applicants may be required to complete a police check and other pre-employment checks. Information provided will be treated in line with our Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Head of Environmental Monitoring, Analytics and Insights
jobs.description:
**Overview**
------------

**Work Type:** Ongoing - Full-time

**Salary:** $193,946 - $263,771

**Grade:** VPS 7

**Occupation:** Science and research

**Location:** Melbourne - Northern suburbs

**Reference:** 1834

**Role details:** Ongoing, full time | VPS 7 | $193,946 to $263,771 + 12% superannuation | Ernest Jones Drive in Macleod, VIC 3085

  

* **Lead environmental monitoring, analytics and insights**
* **Modernise EPA’s science, digital and AI capability**
* **Turn complex evidence into actionable regulatory insights**
  

**About the organisation**

Environment Protection Authority Victoria (EPA) is Victoria’s independent environmental regulator, working to prevent and reduce the harmful effects of pollution and waste on communities and the environment. Operating under the Environment Protection Act 2017, EPA works with communities, government and industry to protect human health and the environment through proactive, risk-based regulation.

  

**About the role**

As Head of Environmental Monitoring, Analytics and Insights, you will lead the modernisation of EPA’s environmental and public health monitoring, analytics and insights functions. Reporting to the Chief Environmental Scientist, you will establish and lead EPA’s Science Digital Enablement Strategy, strengthening the organisation’s ability to collect, manage, analyse, forecast and communicate evidence about risks arising from pollution and waste.

  

You will build and lead the Environmental Monitoring, Analytics and Insights Branch as EPA’s centre of capability for environmental monitoring, forecasting, field investigation, emergency response, surveillance, sensor innovation, digital products and environmental intelligence. You will establish enterprise-wide frameworks and standards, strengthen scientific integrity and quality assurance, and guide the responsible adoption of emerging technologies, including data, digital tools and AI.

  

Working across EPA and with government, academia, industry, research organisations and technology providers, you will develop the partnerships, infrastructure and innovation ecosystems needed to support evidence-based regulation and EPA’s future Centre of Excellence for Regulatory Science and Innovation.

  

**About you**

You are an accomplished senior leader with experience leading complex scientific, digital, environmental, public health, emergency or regulatory functions. You have successfully established or modernised multidisciplinary capabilities, operating models, governance frameworks, digital strategies or science programs within a complex public sector, regulatory or scientific environment.

  

You understand how to translate strategy into practical roadmaps, governance arrangements, digital products and measurable outcomes. You bring experience leading data, AI, digital or analytics modernisation and can ensure scientific evidence is accessible and useful while protecting its quality, independence and integrity.

  

A credible and influential communicator, you build strategic partnerships, negotiate complex outcomes and communicate scientific, environmental and public health issues clearly to executives, governing boards, government, partners and the community. You will bring sound judgement, strong people leadership and a commitment to building a high-performing, collaborative and accountable culture.

  

**To see the full position description:** **Click Here**

  

**How to apply**

Click **‘Apply’** to submit your application, including a cover letter addressing your experience, the key selection criteria, motivations and suitability for the role, and a resume including contact details for two referees.

  

**Applications close Sunday 29 November 2026 at 11:59pm.**

jobs.title: Principal or Technical Director Contaminated Land Human Health and Ecological Risk Assessor
jobs.description:
ERM is seeking a highly experienced Principal or Technical Director level Contaminated Land Human Health and Ecological Risk Assessor to join our Australian contaminated land team and global network of technical specialists.

The role will lead and deliver complex human health and ecological risk assessments, translating site investigation data and conceptual site models into robust, practical advice that supports remediation, development, due diligence and regulatory decision-making in onshore and offshore environments.

**The role**

* Lead complex human health and ecological risk assessments predominantly within Australia and Asia more broadly.
* Develop and critically review conceptual site models, exposure pathways and risk-based assessment levels.
* Provide specialist advice across contaminated land investigation, remediation and management.
* Provide national and international technical leadership, peer review and mentoring.
* Support our Environmental Auditors’ as part of their expert teams, including critical review of assessor technical reports.
* Collaborate with specialists across Australia and internationally, bringing global expertise and leading practice to complex client challenges.

**About you**

* 15+ years’ relevant experience, with strong contaminated land risk assessment expertise.
* Relevant environmental science, toxicology, chemistry, engineering or related qualification.
* Demonstrated experience in human health and/or ecological risk assessment.
* Experience supporting environmental audits and Environmental Auditor expert teams.
* Strong knowledge of the ASC NEPM, PFAS NEMP and Australian contaminated land regulatory frameworks in multiple jurisdictions.
* Strong technical writing, critical review and client communication skills.
* Certified Environmental Professional (CEnvP), or comparable recognised professional registration, strongly preferred.

This is an opportunity to combine deep technical specialisation with national and international collaboration, contributing to ERM’s global strategy of bringing together technical excellence and strategic insight to solve complex environmental, sustainability and business challenge

***Who We Are:***

*As the world’s leading sustainability consulting firm, ERM is uniquely positioned to contribute to the environment and society through the expertise and energy of our employees worldwide. Sustainability is what we do and is at the heart of both our service offerings and how we operate our business. For our people, our vision means attracting, inspiring, developing and rewarding our people to work with the best clients and on the biggest challenges, thus creating valuable careers. We achieve our vision in a sustainable manner by maintaining and living our ERM beliefs that include Together we Challenge, Expertise is our Superpower, and Impact Ignites us.*
